classical_baseline: The classical baseline is the Hedge algorithm of Freund and Schapire, including its sampled variant for active betting, and for the learning part the classical Sparsitron algorithm of Klivans and Meka. The paper also compares against a classical approximate Sparsitron that estimates inner products instead of computing them exactly.
classical_baseline_quotes: A paradigmatic algorithm for online learning is the Hedge algorithm by Freund and Schapire.
We present a classical approximate Sparsitron algorithm, which estimates the inner products instead of computing them exactly (Theorem 6).
classical_difficulty: Classically, the Hedge algorithm has runtime O(TN) because each of the T rounds requires updating N probabilities. For the learning problem, the original Sparsitron has runtime O(N×T×M), and the paper notes that the approximate classical version still has substantial N-dependence. The paper also says the inverse Ising problem has hard sample-complexity lower bounds and that for general graphs the best known classical method is exhaustive search costing N^d.
classical_difficulty_quotes: The run time of the classical algorithm is given by O (T N). At every step, the algorithm updates N probabilities and there are T steps overall.
For learning Ising models on general graphs with N nodes of degree at most d, the best known method is based on exhaustive search costing N d.
An unconditional lower bound on the sample complexity of learning Ising models with N vertices was given by Santhanam and Wainwright [21].
business_stakes: The paper explicitly ties the hedging setting to sports betting and stock market trading, and says transaction costs matter when allocating bets or buying stocks. It also says the speedups may be relevant for hedging risks.
business_stakes_quotes: For example, buying even a single stock on the stock market comes with the cost of contacting a broker and a broker fee.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in the abstract and introduction; finance framing is mainly hedging/stock-market trading rather than a detailed asset-pricing problem.
